Plot the Pareto k values of leave-one-out cross-validation

Source: R/plot-loo.R
plot_loo.Rd

plot_loo() plots the Pareto k value of each site from loo.bef_fit(), together with the threshold above which the leave-one-out estimate for a site is not reliable. The threshold depends on the number of posterior draws and is computed as in the loo package. Sites above the threshold are labeled.

Usage

plot_loo(x, loo = NULL, label = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

A bef_fit object created by bayes_efron_fit().

loo

An optional loo object, the result of loo.bef_fit() for x. If NULL (the default), it is computed.

label

If TRUE (the default), the sites above the threshold are labeled.

...

These dots are for future extensions and must be empty.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

For \(S\) posterior draws, the threshold is \(\min(1 - 1 / \log_{10} S, 0.7)\) (Vehtari et al., 2024). This is 0.7 for about 2,200 draws or more, and 0.656 for the 800 draws of the fits stored in the package.

Removing a site that is above the threshold would change the posterior distribution considerably, so the leave-one-out estimate for that site should not be trusted. See vignette("diagnostics") for a discussion of this check.

The Pareto k values can take some time to compute when there are many sites. To avoid computing them again, pass a result of loo.bef_fit() as loo. This function requires the loo package.

References

Vehtari, A., Simpson, D., Gelman, A., Yao, Y. and Gabry, J. (2024). Pareto smoothed importance sampling. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 25(72), 1-58.

See also

loo.bef_fit(), compare_efron_grids(), vignette("plots")

Examples

plot_loo(krw_fit)


# Reuse a result that was computed earlier.
result <- loo::loo(raudenbush_fit)
plot_loo(raudenbush_fit, loo = result)
